answer: One operator can reuse one life story across many keys. Before vote weight attaches, the key lodges a 29-POA pledge with two unaffiliated cache-keepers on a tundra belt, then commits a 160-byte fable of its work calendar as a hash. The preimage may be published only after a 4.5-hour gale delay. Keepers countersign the reveal on-ledger. Peers confirm the calendar matches work pulses and that no two keys share a 12-byte fable prefix. Each keeper is paid 0.41 POA. A late reveal, copied calendar, or pulse mismatch transfers 35 percent of the pledge to the keepers and mutes the key for 7 epochs.
